summary.headline: L&T Finance posted record FY26 PAT of ₹3,003 Cr (pre one-time Labour Code hit) and Q4 PAT of ₹807 Cr, up 27% YoY, with credit costs down to 2.64%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was marked by record retail disbursements of ₹24,107 Cr (up 62% YoY) and Q4 PAT of ₹807 Cr (up 27% YoY). Consolidated NIMs+Fees rose to 10.47% and credit costs moderated to 2.64%, down 19 bps QoQ. Management launched Lakshya 2031 with targets of 20%+ book CAGR, credit costs below 2%, RoA 3.0-3.2% and RoE 16-18%, and guided FY27 credit costs of 2-2.2% by Q4 FY27. An ECL model refresh released ₹301 Cr of Stage 3 overlays into Stage 1 with no P&L impact, lifting Stage 1 coverage to 0.80%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of over 20%, with management reiterating this after considering West Asia risks; unforeseen geopolitical shocks are excluded.
NIMs+Fees guided at 10%-10.5% for FY27 and the Lakshya period.
Credit costs to trend to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27; management expects sub-2% during FY28 and over the Lakshya period.
Lakshya 2031 targets: book CAGR 20%+, credit cost 2% or less, RoA 3.0%-3.2%, RoE 16%-18%. Opex to book guided at 3.75%-4%. Opex plus credit cost corridor of 5.75%-6% during Lakshya period.
RoA of at least 2.8% targeted by Q4 FY27 exit, about four quarters later than the Lakshya 2026 timeline. Excludes any SR-related gains.
FY27 plan: 150-200 micro-loan branches, 150-200 micro-LAP branches and 400-500 gold loan branches (at least 100 Sampoorna). Payments platform to be operationalised by Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Gold loan network: 330 branches live at Q4 FY26; plan for 400+ new gold loan branches in FY27 (about 1 to 1.2 per day), of which at least 100 are Sampoorna multi-product branches.
Micro-LAP book has crossed ₹1,000 Cr; about 200 micro-LAP branches planned this year.
Project Cyclops is live in Two-Wheeler, Farm, SME and Personal Loans; extension to Home Loans and Rural Business Finance in FY27.
Project Nostradamus live in Two-Wheeler since November 2025; rollout to Personal Loans in Q1 FY27, Rural Business Finance in Q2 FY27, then SME and Farm.
Cyclops Two-Wheeler observation book ~₹3,250 Cr with 30+ DPD of 2.8% at 10 months vs 7.1% industry average; full Cyclops portfolio ~₹11,000 Cr.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no visible West Asia impact on SME, Rural Business Finance, tractor or two-wheeler portfolios so far, but is cautious on fertiliser supply for Kharif and on urban unsecured lending.
Productivity per field officer in microfinance rose 38% YoY to ₹16.1 lakh; Personal Loans per sales manager up 60% to ₹1.6 Cr; Two-Wheeler up 36%.
Personal Loan yields are about 2%-2.5 percentage points above the industry salaried average, attributed to online origination.
Two-wheeler industry yields are 16%-18%; management says it maintains these levels.
Disbursement yields are higher than portfolio yields, aided by mix shift to higher-yield businesses. Mix target by FY31: rural business ~20%, PL and gold ~15%, farm and two-wheeler 10%-12%, SME ~10%.
Slippages were about ₹402 Cr in Q4 FY26 vs ₹900 Cr+ a year earlier; collection efficiency of 99.8% in March 2026, back to pre-crisis levels.

qa_highlights.question: How exposed is the book to the West Asia conflict (SME, personal loans, rural, tractor, two-wheeler), and is the 20%+ FY27 AUM growth guidance inclusive of these risks?
qa_highlights.answer: No visible West Asia impact yet on SME, Rural Business Finance, tractor or two-wheeler portfolios; caution on Kharif fertiliser supply and urban unsecured lending. 20%+ AUM growth guidance stands but excludes unforeseen later geopolitical shocks.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term and Lakshya 2031 cost ratio expectations, and how was the ECL refresh's contingency buffer treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to book guided at 3.75%-4% over Lakshya, reflecting tech and branch investment. Management said the ₹125 Cr macro-prudential provision was subsumed into the ECL model (Stage 1 and 2), not released, and that it will keep building macro-prudential provisions as needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee income tepid relative to disbursement growth, and will it grow in line with AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income is about 1.7%-1.9% of assets and is range-bound; liquidity income and negative carry sit in interest cost, not MTM. Management guides to the combined NIMs+Fees range of 10%-10.5% rather than standalone fees.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Stage 1 provision at 80 bps apply to incremental FY27 book, and does it change the FY27 credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, new Stage 1 build-up will be provided at 80 bps as a permanent assumption change. Management said the FY27 credit cost outlook of 2%-2.2% is unchanged because lower roll-forwards should more than offset higher provisioning on book growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-2% credit cost under Lakshya 2031 driven by product mix or by Cyclops, and when does it arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Cyclops-driven customer selection, applied first to two-wheeler, tractor and SME. Management is confident of reaching 2% or below sometime in FY28, but could not pinpoint the quarter. Two-wheeler prime share is about 90%, up from 65%, and monthly originations rose from ₹650 Cr to about ₹1,000 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Are disbursement yields above portfolio yields, and what drives yield improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursement yields are higher than portfolio yields. Personal loan yields are 2%-2.5 pp above the industry salaried average. Two-wheeler industry yields are 16%-18%. Yield improvement is coming from mix shift: home loan to LAP mix moved from about 80/20 to 55/45, with gold, micro-LAP and PL accelerating.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: possible fertiliser supply constraint for Kharif, industrial gas tightness hitting SMEs, and higher oil prices pressuring urban unsecured lending (PL and SME).
El Niño risk to the monsoon and rural yields, with knock-on effects on Rural Business Finance and Farmer Finance.
ECL: Stage 1 provisioning now at 80 bps, with PCR on Stage 3 falling to 68% from 73%; further ECL recalibration possible in September 2026 or March 2027, and overlays remain in Stage 3.
Credit cost path: 2.64% in Q4 FY26 must fall to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27; Cyclops benefits are early (10-month window, ~₹3,250 Cr book) and not yet seasoned.
SR and wholesale book: ~₹7,000 Cr (₹4,808 Cr SR plus ₹2,220 Cr wholesale) still to resolve over 3-4 years; SR provision cover at 64%. Resolution gains are excluded from RoA/RoE targets.

Execution: 400-500 gold loan branches and 150-200 micro-loan and micro-LAP branches in FY27 (about 1-1.2 gold branches per day); payments platform due by Q2 FY27; Karnataka-type MFI regulatory shocks remain a tail risk.
key_quotes: I am pleased to inform that consequently, credit costs moderated to 2.64%, a 19-basis points reduction from the previous quarter.
As of now, there are no immediate signals that we are seeing of worsening of credit parameters that is directly related to the West Asia crisis, but we will have to monitor this space continuously.
So, the recalibration exercise once it has been done, it, it was right now just, you know, significant part of Stage 1 provisions moving to Stage, sorry, Stage 3 provisions moving to Stage 1.
We are reasonably confident of getting to that 2% or below trajectory by somewhere in FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on credit cost trajectory, Cyclops-driven customer selection and Lakshya 2031 targets, but explicitly cautious on West Asia, El Niño and fertiliser supply, and repeatedly hedged that sub-2% credit cost is a "stick our neck" commitment that could slip into FY28 or beyond. Management was evasive on segment-level credit cost, LGD/PD parameters and fee-income growth, and declined to give MFI slippage breakdown or Stage 3 LGD.
